service-workers/service-worker/unregiste.description: Runs until the maximum duration of the runner (1 minute): Clear-Site-Data is not implemented, so it cannot abort the evaluation of a service worker script that loops forever

fetch/content-encoding/gzip/big-gzip-bod.description: Runs ~45 seconds, close to the maximum duration of the runner (1 minute), so it times out randomly: the test reads a decoded body of 27 MB through a BYOB reader in chunks of at most 64 KB, then hashes it; it passes when it completes

fetch/content-encoding/br/big-br-body.ht.description: Runs ~45 seconds, close to the maximum duration of the runner (1 minute), so it times out randomly: the test reads a decoded body of 27 MB through a BYOB reader in chunks of at most 64 KB, then hashes it; it passes when it completes

html/semantics/tabular-data/processing-m.description: the test adds 131,000 table rows and reads the geometry after each addition: the styles and the layout of the whole document are computed again (there is no incremental style and layout), ~60 s, so it times out randomly

dom/nodes/NodeList-static-length-getter-.description: JavaScript engine stress test (millions of property accesses in a loop, ~18 seconds per test alone in a Release build): too slow for every run, and it does not test the DOM

encoding/legacy-mb-japanese/*.description: Too slow for every run (~650,000 subtests, each variant decodes 1,000 characters with iframes, ~2 minutes) and most of them time out: the runner decodes the documents of the iframes as UTF-8 (#82). The encoders and decoders are tested by the unit tests and by legacy-mb-schinese

html/webappapis/scripting/events/compile.description: Runs until the maximum duration of the runner (1 minute): a test needs window.open() and never completes, while another one reloads the iframe from its load event handler, so the event loop is never idle and the harness timeout (virtual clock) never fires

html/semantics/permission-element/*.description: the permission elements (`<permission>`, `<geolocation>`, `<install>`, `<usermedia>`, camera/microphone) proposed by the WICG Page Embedded Permission Control incubation: they are not part of the HTML Standard, and only Chromium implements them; most of the tests check their rendering (reftests, bounded CSS properties, icons) or need permission prompts

fetch/security/dangling-markup/dangling-.description: the dangling markup mitigation is not implemented: the requests of the URLs that contain a newline and `<` are not blocked, so the service worker of the test records them too, and the test reads the recorded requests as soon as there are as many as its resources (11): depending on the timing, the requests of the `meta` refresh and of the `iframe` are not recorded yet (ERROR) or they are (PASS)

css/css-masking/clip-path/animations/cli.description: reftest whose screenshot is taken in the animation frame after the effect of the animation is replaced: depending on the timing of the frames, the first or the second step of the new effect is painted

mathml/relations/css-styling/mozilla-393.description: reftest whose result depends on the platform: the glyphs are antialiased by the font engine of the platform (CoreText, FreeType, DirectWrite), so it passes on Linux and fails on macOS or the reverse

speculation-rules/prerender/service-work.description: Two subtests register a service worker and create the prerendered page without waiting for the worker to be activated: a navigation is only controlled by an active worker, so when the activation is slower than the prerendering (on the loaded CI agents), the prerendered page is not controlled and its fetch of ping gets 404 Not Found instead of pong
